headline: Social contracts are the agreements—explicit and implicit—that make living together possible
universal_truth: Society runs on agreements; most aren't written down but are understood and expected
fun_facts: Philosophers like Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau developed social contract theory
Most social agreements are implicit—never stated but understood
Breaking unwritten rules often carries social rather than legal consequences
discussion_questions: What unwritten rules govern your interactions?
When have you seen social contracts broken?
How do implicit agreements differ from explicit ones?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Most rules aren't laws. They're agreements—spoken or unspoken—about how we'll treat each other. Don't cut in line. Return borrowed things. Keep promises. These social contracts enable cooperation without enforcement.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Why do people follow rules that aren't enforced by law?

options.text: Social contracts enable cooperation—breaking them invites social consequences and erodes trust; we follow unwritten rules because life works better when people can rely on each other
options.response: Yes. Social rules run on reputation and relationship. Break them and others stop cooperating with you. Keep them and you're trusted, included, helped. Society is mutual rule-following.
Pressure is the enforcement mechanism, but the rules themselves enable the trust that makes society work...

q1.title: Implicit Agreements
q1.script: Most social rules aren't discussed—they're understood. You learned them growing up. The fact that they're implicit makes them powerful. You follow rules you never consciously agreed to.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Implicit Agreements"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Trust Foundation
q2.script: Social contracts build trust. When everyone follows the rules, you can rely on others. This trust is society's foundation. Widespread rule-breaking collapses cooperation.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Renegotiating Rules
q3.script: Social contracts can change. What was expected in one era might not be in another. As society evolves, implicit agreements get questioned and renegotiated. This is healthy.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Society runs on agreements. Most aren't written down but are understood and expected. Honor the contracts that make cooperation possible.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 336. Tomorrow, we'll explore how people trade. Until then, notice the unwritten rules you follow.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Social Contract Awareness - What Rules Do You Follow?
growTrack.activity: What unwritten rules govern your daily life? Make a list of social expectations you follow that aren't laws. Which do you think are valuable? Which might need renegotiating?
